Follow the prescribed dosage.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: those hypersensitive to this medicine; hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; infants under 12 months; hyperkalemia; Wilson's disease; hemochromatosis (iron deposits in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism); hemosiderosis; non-iron-deficiency anemia; kidney stones; severe renal failure; or hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you have hyperoxaluria (excess oxalate excreted in urine); are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis; cardiac/circulatory dysfunction; renal impairment; hypoproteinemia; gallbladder-related disease; liver disease; gallbladder obstruction; copper deficiency; alkalosis; diabetes; gout, kidney stones, or a history of kidney stones; or are hypersensitive or allergic to Yellow No. 5. en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for supplementation of vitamin D during pregnancy/lactation, growth periods, and old age and for prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets, and for calcium deficiency and other calcium supplementation.
en.usage:
Ages 8 and older and adults: take 1 tablet once daily.
Follow the prescribed dosage.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: those hypersensitive to this medicine; infants under 12 months; hypercalcemia; sarcoidosis; kidney disease; kidney stones; or severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you are an infant under 1 year; a patient under a doctor's care; a child who gets much sunlight and eats normally; are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; premature infants, infants; cardiac/circulatory dysfunction; renal impairment; hypoproteinemia; being treated with cardiac glycosides; or have a history of kidney stones.

Follow the prescribed dosage and usage.

When administering to children, do so under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracyclines, or antacids. Taking with antialdosterone agents or triamterene may cause hyperkalemia, so use caution. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, cardiac arrest, or central nervous system depression occur, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist. If you accidentally overdose, or if there is no improvement after about a month of use, stop immediately and consult a pharmacist.

en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment for damaged hair, non-infectious poor nail growth, and hair loss.
en.usage:
Adults: take 1 capsule 3 times daily; children aged 12 and older: take 1 capsule once or twice daily after meals.

Follow the prescribed dosage.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: those hypersensitive to this medicine; children under 12 years; hair loss due to scarring; androgenetic (hereditary) alopecia; or male-pattern baldness.

Consult a pharmacist before use if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding.

Consult a pharmacist when using with sulfonamide preparations.
